---
title: Animations in VS Code
---

If you are coding using Jupyter notebooks in VS Code, then
it is possible to create animations by importing the
`HTML` class from the IPython module.  See the code
snippet below for an example

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.animation as animation
from IPython.display import HTML

# create independent variables
t = np.logspace(-2, 1, 30)
x = np.linspace(-3, 3, 300)

# create function to plot
u = lambda t: 1 / np.sqrt(4 * np.pi * t) * np.exp(-x**2 / 4 / t)

# plot the first time point
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
line = plt.plot(x, u(t[0]), lw = 2, color = 'k')[0]

# edit the figure properties
ax.set(
    xlim = [-3, 3], 
    ylim = [0, 3], 
    xlabel = '$x$', 
    ylabel = '$u(x,t)$'
    )

def update(frame):
    """
    Define a function to update the figure.  Here,
    frame is an integer that is used to update the
    data in the plot.  In this case, frame is used
    to increment time
    """    
    line.set_ydata(u(t[frame]))
    ax.set_title(f'$t = {t[frame]:.3f}$')
    return line

# animate
ani = animation.FuncAnimation(fig = fig, func = update, frames = 30)
HTML(ani.to_jshtml())  # Embed animation as HTML5
```
